scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Three virtual loopback interfaces — lo1, lo2, and lo3 — on r12, which are the physical sources of the EIGRP-advertised prefixes 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, and 102.1.4.0/24 respectively.

**Mechanism:** In FRR EIGRP, a `network` statement only causes a prefix to be originated if the matching interface has an up/connected route. When lo1/lo2/lo3 are down, the kernel removes their connected routes and FRR EIGRP withdraws (or never advertises) those three prefixes. r12's EIGRP topology table confirms this — it contains only `102.1.1.0/24 via Connected, lo` (the one loopback that is UP). r11, which peers with r12 via EIGRP over segment EE (112.0.0.0/8), never receives update advertisements for the three missing prefixes, so they do not enter r11's EIGRP table. Since r11 also does `redistribute eigrp` into OSPF area 3, those three prefixes are never injected as AS-External LSAs. r1, which reaches r11 through OSPF area 3 (111.0.0.0/8, eth1), therefore has no OSPF route for 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, or 102.1.4.0/24 — while 102.1.1.0/24 (sourced from `lo` which is UP) propagates normally.

**Localization:** r12 — interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3. All three show `flags: <BROADCAST,NOARP>` (no UP/RUNNING), `Link ups: 0 (never)`, `Link downs: 1 at 2026/08/04 10:39:34`.

**Root cause:** r12's loopback interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 are in a persistent down state, eliminating the connected routes for 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, and 102.1.4.0/24 from the EIGRP domain.

**Fix:** Bring the interfaces up on r12: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`. Once up, EIGRP will re-advertise the three prefixes, r11 will redistribute them into OSPF, and all four 102.1.x.0/24 routes will appear in r1's RIB.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly localizes the fault to r12, stating lo1/lo2/lo3 on r12 are down.
The report explicitly identifies the loopback dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 on r12 as the affected components.

The report explicitly identifies that lo1/lo2/lo3 were withdrawn while lo remained up, causing three prefixes to be withdrawn by EIGRP while 102.1.1.0/24 stayed advertised (partial-withdrawal pattern).
Correctly instructs to bring lo1/lo2/lo3 up on r12 (ip link set ... up), which will restore the connected routes and cause EIGRP to advertise the missing prefixes.

The investigation log contains concrete outputs showing lo1/lo2/lo3 on r12 are down and r12's EIGRP topology only lists 102.1.1.0/24; the agent also checked for upstream filtering on r11/r1. There is a small timeline inconsistency (an earlier snapshot showed all four prefixes present on r1/r11) which slightly weakens the causal narrative but does not undercut the core observation that r12's down interfaces remove the connected routes and thus the EIGRP-originated prefixes.
